{
  "ambiguities": [],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the exact value asserted for both the infimum and the norm of an optimal perturbation.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For any natural dimensions m,n, real m-by-n matrix A, and b in R^m, define c(A,b)=0 if b=0, and c(A,b)=||A^T b||_2/||b||_2 otherwise.",
      "name": "Claimed optimal perturbation size",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "With y=0 and δb=0, requires the zero vector to minimize the least-squares objective for A+ΔA and the unchanged right-hand side b.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For any m,n, A in R^(m×n), b in R^m, y in R^n, ΔA in R^(m×n), and δb in R^m, P(A,b,y,ΔA,δb) means that y is a global least-squares minimizer for the matrix A+ΔA and right-hand side b+δb. Both additions are entrywise.",
      "name": "Perturbed least-squares feasibility",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the perturbation measure as the absolute Frobenius norm.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For every real m-by-n matrix A, define ||A||_F=sqrt(Σ_i Σ_j A_ij^2), with indices i in Fin m and j in Fin n.",
      "name": "Frobenius norm",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target evaluates this quantity at y=0 and identifies it with c(A,b).",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b,y of the indicated dimensions, define β(A,b,y) as the real infimum of S(A,b,y), the set of Frobenius norms of matrix perturbations making y a least-squares minimizer while leaving b fixed.",
      "name": "Infimal matrix perturbation size",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes feasibility a global minimization condition over every competitor in R^n.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b and x in R^n, x is a least-squares minimizer precisely when, for every z in R^n, Q(A,b,x)≤Q(A,b,z).",
      "name": "Global least-squares minimizer",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the squared quantity underlying the Frobenius norm.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For any real m-by-n matrix A, return Σ_{i in Fin m} Σ_{j in Fin n} A_ij^2.",
      "name": "Sum of squared matrix entries",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the precise feasible norm set whose infimum appears in the target; only the matrix is perturbed.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b,y, S(A,b,y)={η in R : there exists ΔA in R^(m×n) such that P(A,b,y,ΔA,0) and η=||ΔA||_F}.",
      "name": "Attainable perturbation norms",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the vector in the numerator of c(A,b).",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b, return the vector A^T b in R^n whose j-th coordinate is Σ_{i in Fin m} A_ij b_i.",
      "name": "Transpose matrix-vector product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies Euclidean norms in both numerator and denominator of c(A,b).",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For every natural n and vector x in R^n, define ||x||_2=sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin n} x_i^2).",
      "name": "Euclidean vector norm",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies the exact objective used in all minimization predicates.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b and x in R^n, define Q(A,b,x)=Σ_{i in Fin m} ((Ax)_i-b_i)^2=||Ax-b||_2^2.",
      "name": "Squared residual objective",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Underlies both the Euclidean norm and the least-squares objective.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For every natural n and x in R^n, return Σ_{i in Fin n} x_i^2.",
      "name": "Sum of squared vector coordinates",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the residual used to define least-squares minimization.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "For any m,n,A,b,x, return the vector r(A,b,x) in R^m with r_i=(Ax)_i-b_i.",
      "name": "Residual vector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies ordinary finite-dimensional matrix action in the objective.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "For any m,n, A in R^(m×n), and x in R^n, return Ax in R^m with (Ax)_i=Σ_{j in Fin n} A_ij x_j.",
      "name": "Matrix-vector product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Requires the infimum identity and witness existence simultaneously, and requires every listed property of that witness.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "For propositions a and b, And(a,b) is their conjunction: both a and b hold.",
      "name": "Logical conjunction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses exact scalar equalities, vector equality to zero, and equality between a feasible set element and a perturbation norm.",
      "id": "D015",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort α and any x,y in α, Eq(x,y) asserts that x and y are equal.",
      "name": "Equality",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Quantifies the optimal matrix perturbation and the matrix witnesses defining attainable norm values.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort α and predicate p on α, Exists(p) asserts that some x in α satisfies p(x).",
      "name": "Existential quantification",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the row and column index sets and permits zero-dimensional matrices and vectors.",
      "id": "D017",
      "meaning": "For each natural n, Fin n is the finite type of natural indices 0 through n−1; Fin 0 is empty.",
      "name": "Finite coordinate index type",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses n≤m, least-squares objective comparisons, and the optimal perturbation norm inequality.",
      "id": "D018",
      "meaning": "For any type α equipped with a relation LE, this projection returns its binary relation ≤ on α.",
      "name": "Less-than-or-equal relation projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes dimensions nonnegative integers and supplies natural exponents.",
      "id": "D019",
      "meaning": "Nat is the type of natural numbers including zero.",
      "name": "Natural numbers",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the numeral 0 in real and vector types and the exponent 2 as a natural number.",
      "id": "D020",
      "meaning": "For any type α, natural number k, and an OfNat α k instance, return the element of α designated by the numeral k.",
      "name": "Numeral interpretation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes each vector written as 0 identically zero in every coordinate.",
      "id": "D021",
      "meaning": "For any index type ι and family of types M(i), each equipped with a zero, the dependent function space has zero given by the function i↦0 in M(i).",
      "name": "Pointwise zero function",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "All matrix entries, vector coordinates, objectives, norms, infima, and optimal values are real.",
      "id": "D022",
      "meaning": "Real is the type of real numbers.",
      "name": "Real scalar domain",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures objective and norm comparisons use the ordinary real order.",
      "id": "D023",
      "meaning": "Supplies the usual relation ≤ on the real numbers.",
      "name": "Real order instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies scalar zero and the coordinate values of every zero vector.",
      "id": "D024",
      "meaning": "Supplies the real number zero as the distinguished zero element of R.",
      "name": "Real zero instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Connects written zero numerals to the real and pointwise vector zeros.",
      "id": "D025",
      "meaning": "For any type α with a distinguished zero, interprets the numeral 0 as that zero.",
      "name": "Zero numeral instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the dimension hypothesis the usual natural-number inequality n≤m.",
      "id": "D026",
      "meaning": "Supplies the ordinary less-than-or-equal relation on natural numbers.",
      "name": "Natural-number order instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Exposes the real division operation used in c(A,b).",
      "id": "D027",
      "meaning": "For any type G equipped with a division-and-inverse monoid structure, extracts its division operation.",
      "name": "Division structure projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Allows exhaustive sums over all row and column indices and finite-coordinate equality decisions.",
      "id": "D028",
      "meaning": "For every natural n, supplies an enumeration of Fin n by 0,…,n−1, with no repetitions and containing every element.",
      "name": "Finite enumeration of coordinates",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the logical decision of whether the finite real vector b equals zero for the conditional defining c(A,b).",
      "id": "D029",
      "meaning": "For any finite type α and family β(a) with decidable equality in every fiber, gives decidable equality of dependent functions f,g by checking f(a)=g(a) for all a in the finite enumeration.",
      "name": "Equality decision for finite functions",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Applies addition to entries when forming the perturbed matrix and right-hand side.",
      "id": "D030",
      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ with a heterogeneous addition operation α×β→γ, extracts that operation.",
      "name": "Addition operation projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Forms the norm ratio in the nonzero-b branch of c(A,b).",
      "id": "D031",
      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ with a heterogeneous division operation α×β→γ, extracts that operation.",
      "name": "Division operation projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Applies the real set-infimum operation to S(A,b,y). The operation's type alone does not assert attainment.",
      "id": "D032",
      "meaning": "For any type α equipped with an InfSet structure, extracts its operation taking a subset of α to its designated infimum value in α.",
      "name": "Set-infimum operation projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the exact zero test in c(A,b); it introduces no floating-point or numerical approximation model.",
      "id": "D033",
      "meaning": "For any two real numbers a,b, supplies a decision of a=b obtained from the real linear-order structure.",
      "name": "Real equality decision",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the perturbations additive using ordinary real addition.",
      "id": "D034",
      "meaning": "Supplies ordinary addition of real numbers.",
      "name": "Real addition instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the ordinary real quotient in c(A,b). Its denominator is positive in the branch where b≠0.",
      "id": "D035",
      "meaning": "Equips R with its multiplicative monoid and inverse, division defined by a/b=a·b⁻¹, and recursively defined integer powers, together with the corresponding laws.",
      "name": "Real division and inverse structure",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines β using the real infimum rather than an extended-real value. Here its feasible set is nonempty and bounded below.",
      "id": "D036",
      "meaning": "Defines the real set-infimum operation by sInf(S)=−sSup(−S), where −S={−s : s∈S}. For nonempty real sets bounded below, this is the usual greatest lower bound.",
      "name": "Real infimum instance",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Turns nonnegative sums of squares into the Euclidean and Frobenius norms.",
      "id": "D037",
      "meaning": "For every real x, first convert x to the nonnegative real max(x,0), apply the nonnegative-real square-root map, and return its real value. Thus this is the nonnegative square root for x≥0 and zero for x<0.",
      "name": "Real square root",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Connects addition notation in the perturbation predicate to real addition.",
      "id": "D038",
      "meaning": "For any type α with addition, provides heterogeneous-addition notation with both inputs and output in α, using the same addition.",
      "name": "Homogeneous addition adapter",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Connects division notation in c(A,b) to real division.",
      "id": "D039",
